title: Ephemeral fail-shepherd and weighted evictor fastpatch
author: Marina Chen
release_notes: Hotfix: introduce ephemeral quiet-window and weighted-evictor to reduce SLO breaches during transient KV stalls; backported to release/2026-02 for affected customers.
description: Motivation: Following a regional incident (SUP-9876) where short-lived KV-stalls amplified into tenant SLO violations, we need a fast, low-risk mitigation that prevents circuit thrash and evens tenant fairness without a heavy config rollout. This PR adds a lightweight 'fail-shepherd' controller that gates transient circuit flips using a short, adjustable quiet-window and couples it with a weighted-evictor that preferentially trims noisy tenants under egress pressure. Design summary: 1) Quiet-window: newly added per-region ephemeral timer (default 8s) that suppresses immediate reopen attempts after a circuit trip to avoid rapid flip cycles; 2) Adaptive reopen pacing: reopen attempts are backoff-capped and attempt counts are recorded in ephemeral metrics for telemetry-driven tuning; 3) Weighted evictor: eviction decisions now consider tenant weight and recent token-rate variance to avoid evicting small fair tenants when a noisy tenant spikes; weights default to usage but can be overridden by tenant config; 4) KV-coalescer soft-handoff: when a node drains KV pressure, we wait for a short grace window to preserve prefix cache affinity for hottenants; 5) Telemetry hooks: emit quiet_window.* and evictor.* metrics and an incident log marker for correlation with trace ids. Checklist: - [x] implement quiet-window timer and secure expiration path; - [x] integrate weighted evictor into admission pipeline; - [x] emit metrics for SLO dashboards; - [x] add unit tests for timer semantics and eviction scoring; - [x] run staged canary in us-west-2 on dedicated dev fleet; - [x] backport to release/2026-02. Risk: low surface area change (control-plane gating + small admission path hook). No model-serving code changes. Rollout: staged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full; automatic rollback if SLO regressions exceed 0.5 p50 latency or 2% error-rate bump in canary windows. Related: ENG-4521 explains long-term plan to replace static thresholds with learned reopen schedules.
